feature_contract.goal: Restore the projected per-vehicle rank marker's complete integer and subpixel position through the original clip and animated quad siblings while preserving spatial stereo eye ownership, unrelated NaviPub and screen ranking.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only the four exact vehicle rank clip producers and their queued kind-0 SPRARGS/kind-1 SPRARGS2 siblings; never other menu sprites, NaviPub, start shadow, GOAL, lenses or alternative backends.
trace_stages: Original vehicle Calc3D2D fractional world projection feeds RankMarker_putClipSprite and snapshots per-vehicle TLS projected anchor before the original clip call.
Original put_clip_sprite queues zero or more SpriteNode children by sprite priority; kind-0 uses SPRARGS float24/float28 and kind-1 uses SPRARGS2 affine quad mtx_14 translation _41/_42.

After original producer returns, the bounded sibling walk restores the captured fractional coordinate before TagAppendedNodes assigns the same projected-world semantic and the R26/R30 per-eye draw consumes it.
subcomponents: Preserve frozen per-car fractional X/Y across nested original clip producer calls and every newly appended priority sibling.
Restore both kind-0 clip and kind-1 animated affine-quad positions atomically with finite checks while leaving UV/quad scale, unknown layouts and other sprites unchanged.
Retain projected-world marker semantics and explicit ScreenHud/NaviPub fallback without changing left/right head pose or external drawing classes.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: All newly queued kind-0 rank clips preserve the fractional projected car anchor in both X and Y after integer clip placement.
Kind-1 rank marker affine siblings receive the same fractional shift through translation _41/_42 without altering transform scale, UVs or depth.
NaN, infinite, out-of-range fractions, nonfinite coordinates and unrelated sprite node kinds do not result in partial position writes or unrelated HUD alterations.
Validation-bearing GitHub SHA must pass DX9Ex Active game/host/full-chain/package, Domain Isolation and applicable source-impact/HUD checks.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Original RankMarker_putClipSprite emits integer x/y and corrects fractional remainders after put_clip_sprite queues nodes; historical correction only edited kind-0 args_10 while kind-1 animated siblings use separate args2_58.
source_trace: hooks_uiscaling.cpp freezes RankMarkerFracX/Y and RankMarkerProjectedInfo before invoking the original put_clip_sprite to prevent nested TLS producer overwrite.
Game::sprite_prio_root per-priority tails delimit only newly enqueued siblings from that exact original clip producer, which can be kind-0 SPRARGS or kind-1 transformed SPRARGS2.
RestoreFraction now shifts kind-0 float24/float28 or kind-1 mtx_14._41/_42 before TagAppendedNodes carries semantic ownership into downstream stereo per-eye rendering.
diagnosis.root_cause: The historical rank marker fractional position correction updated only kind-0 SPRARGS; an animated rank marker sibling stored its anchor in the kind-1 SPRARGS2 affine translation and therefore remained integer-snapped relative to the projected moving car.
alternatives_rejected: Do not replace Calc3D2D with a global HUD shift or write unrelated rank sprites; that would break individual vehicle-world anchors and NaviPub.
Do not modify affine basis _11/_22 or UV/priority to simulate a fractional translation; moving mtx_14._41/_42 preserves the whole quad.
Do not assume all siblings use the kind-0 node memory layout; kind-1 uses args2_58 and requires a separate case.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Original material SHA 39aa05402fb3fd5327a66c3f30a95474d4e18589 introduces src/vr/game/rank_marker_fraction.hpp, calls RestoreFraction for each exact clip sibling and registers a portable C++ rank-marker smoke test with vrhost CMake.

diagnosis.eye_ownership: Per-eye stereo reprojects each tagged ProjectedWorldMarker2D using its existing Calc3D2D vehicle-relative semantic; code changes producer-space source positions only. Matching Quest3/VDXR visual acceptance remains untested.
